verdict.rationale: Superset documents itself as local-first: it works offline and keeps code on the user's machine. Its CLI manages a 'local host server' that drives the same backend as the desktop app, and the code sits in a public GitHub repo. That means core agent orchestration runs on user-controlled hardware. However, cloud pieces such as sync, remote access and the API/MCP endpoint are hosted at api.superset.sh, and nothing documents self-hosting those. missing for 10: explicit self-hosting docs, an open-source license or deploy guide for the backend/sync service, a self-hosted alternative to the hosted API/MCP endpoint, independent corroboration of a self-hosted deployment.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Superset is local-first: it works offline and syncs when connected. Your code never leaves your machine unless you say so.
Use it to manage workspaces, tasks, automations, and the local host server from your terminal or from CI.
The Superset CLI (`superset`) is a single static binary that drives the same backend as the desktop app.
